sources.cite: ACM/IEEE-CS/AAAI, Computer Science Curricula 2023 (CS2023), knowledge areas (DM: Data Management)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch of the report's first part: 17 knowledge areas, among them DM: Data Management. The fetch reached the table of contents, not the knowledge units' topic lists, so topic detail is from the MSCS course's own dated unit sources (read 2026-11-11, REQ-245). The case's decision: read the plan, see a sequential scan where a function on the column defeats the B-tree index, and add an index that matches the predicate without blocking writes.

Relevant text: scan nodes 'return raw rows from a table'; a sequential scan with a WHERE clause 'checks the condition for each row it scans, and outputs only the ones that pass'; an Index Scan shows 'Index Cond'; with ANALYZE, 'EXPLAIN actually executes the query' and 'Rows Removed by Filter' counts rows a filter rejected. Read through a summarizing fetch of the PostgreSQL 18.7 page on 2026-11-14. The plan lines in the scenario are authored renderings in EXPLAIN's style; the costs and times are invented for the case.

Relevant text: 'a common way to do case-insensitive comparisons is to use the lower function: SELECT * FROM test1 WHERE lower(col1) = 'value'; This query can use an index if one has been defined on the result of the lower(col1) function'; index expressions 'are relatively expensive to maintain' on insert and update. Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-14. Why the existing index on email cannot serve a filter on lower(email).

sources.cite: PostgreSQL 18 Documentation, CREATE INDEX (Building Indexes Concurrently)
sources.note: Relevant text: 'Normally PostgreSQL locks the table to be indexed against writes ... Other transactions can still read the table, but if they try to insert, update, or delete rows in the table they will block until the index build is finished.' With CONCURRENTLY PostgreSQL 'will build the index without taking any locks that prevent concurrent inserts, updates, or deletes', at the cost of two table scans; it 'cannot' run inside a transaction block, and a failed build leaves an 'invalid' index to drop and rebuild. Read through a summarizing fetch of the PostgreSQL 18.7 page on 2026-11-14.

Relevant text: SHARE lock, 'Acquired by CREATE INDEX (without CONCURRENTLY)', 'protects a table against concurrent data changes'; ACCESS EXCLUSIVE (taken by VACUUM FULL among others) conflicts with every lock mode, so even plain SELECTs wait. Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-14 (the ACCESS EXCLUSIVE list was read on the same page).
